wy_cody.blurb: Cody sits in northwest Wyoming east of Yellowstone, and most of the climbing lies in Shoshone Canyon just west of town. The canyon mixes sandstone bouldering, limestone and granite sport climbing, and trad that is mostly on the granite, while the South Fork of the Shoshone River offers ice climbing. Sport routes lead, followed by bouldering, trad and a sizeable ice scene. Roped grades concentrate from 5.10 to 5.12; boulder problems are mostly V0 to V3. Lower Canyon Granite, Cedar Mountain and The Island are the biggest zones. The granite is fractured and featured with good friction. At the lower canyon, spring and fall are best, summer is comfortable, the north side above the road gets good sun and the south wall can be chilly.

nh_merrimack_valley.blurb: The Merrimack Valley is a southern New Hampshire region where bouldering dominates, with a smaller trad scene and a few top-ropes. Boulder problems run V0 to V12 but sit mostly between V0 and V5; roped routes are mostly moderate. Clough State Park is the biggest zone, with good granite boulders, caves and a mix of sun and shade, though big flakes and small crimps can break. Dumplingtown Hill is a short, sunny crag that dries quickly, mixing trad lines, highball gear routes and boulders. Rock Rimmon is a small city cliff of mostly trad and top-rope, from slabs to steeper faces, and is a good place for newer climbers. Palmer Bartell Forest and Beaver Brook add more bouldering.

qc_14_lanaudiere.blurb: Lanaudière covers central Quebec between the Saint Lawrence River and the Laurentian Mountains, with a farmland plain in the south, a lake-dotted foothill belt in the middle and a forested plateau to the north. Sport and trad dominate, with ice and mixed climbing in winter, some bouldering and a few top-ropes. Roped grades center on 5.9 to 5.11 and reach 5.13. Parc de la falaise cachée is the largest area, followed by Les Contreforts, mostly sport, and Lac du Cap, mostly trad. Montagne du Tranchant is the best-known cliff: it faces southwest and dries quickly after rain, and its exfoliating rock means most routes there are sport or mixed.

ky_miller_fork_recreational_preserve_mfr.blurb: Miller Fork lies near Beattyville in the Red River Gorge region of eastern Kentucky. It holds nearly 30 crags and over 500 routes along what is a long cliff line, much of it still undeveloped. Sport climbing dominates, with trad at many crags and a bare handful of boulders. Grades concentrate from 5.10 to 5.12 with a good group at 5.13 and a spread of moderates from 5.7 to 5.9. The biggest crags are The Infirmary, Secret Garden, which carries the most trad, Monastery and Fruit Wall, with Neverland close behind.

_expect.name: Hwy 20 and North Cascades National Park

wa_hwy20_ncnp.blurb: Highway 20 threads the Skagit River Valley, North Cascades National Park and Washington Pass, and the climbing here ranges from roadside crags to big mountain objectives. Alpine routes make up the biggest share, with sport and trad close behind, plus mountaineering, scrambling and a few boulders. Alpine climbing includes snow and ice routes and rock towers, many of them multi-pitch. The cliffs near Newhalem and Diablo in the upper Skagit are solid gneiss with mostly sport. Roped grades concentrate from 5.8 to 5.12. Other Skagit Valley crags and Walker Valley and Lake Cavanaugh Road Crags add lower-elevation options.
